purpose: Primary sources for portfolio-construction subjects Damodaran's Investment Philosophies course does not teach to implementable depth, plus current evidence needed to apply the course. See docs/lesson-plans/portfolio-builder-mission-curriculum.md section 6.

policy.primaryOnly: Every source must be the issuer, regulator, standard-setter, or original author. No commentary, no aggregator, no course-notes mirror. A mirror may be recorded as a fallback but never as the citation.
policy.verifyBeforeAdding: Every URL must be fetch-tested before it enters this file. Search results are unreliable: two candidate URLs returned 404 and one returned 403 during the initial survey.

decay.high: Contains figures that change at least annually (tax thresholds, risk premiums, product costs). Re-fetch and re-verify every 12 months. Never hardcode these numbers into lesson copy — cite them with a date.
decay.medium: Framework or product landscape that drifts over years.
decay.low: Methodology or principles, stable across editions.

policy.jurisdiction: US is the only locked jurisdiction. Sources marked "any" are jurisdiction-neutral. When OPS expands, add sibling entries keyed by jurisdiction and select on the learner's reported status; do not silently show US tax rules to a non-US learner.

sources.subject: allocation-method
sources.title: Vanguard's Principles for Investing Success
sources.teaches: Goals, balance, cost and discipline as an explicit construction framework. Supplies the step Damodaran omits: turning a risk view into an allocation.

sources.subject: rebalancing
sources.title: The Rebalancing Edge: optimizing rebalancing through threshold-based strategies
sources.teaches: Provider-scale evidence about threshold versus calendar rebalancing and the trade between tracking target weights and paying implementation costs. Pairs with mission 8's friction budget as mechanism evidence.
sources.limitation: This is a target-date-fund provider study using daily monitoring and a 200/175-basis-point policy. It is not a DIY personal rebalancing rule and cannot justify prescribing those thresholds to an individual learner.

sources.subject: investment-readiness
sources.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Office of Investor Education and Advocacy
sources.title: Investor Preparedness Checklist
sources.teaches: Goal setting, a savings and investment plan, paying high-interest debt first, employer match, risk tolerance, fees, research, diversification, and fraud awareness.
sources.limitation: A checklist is not an individualized readiness determination. OPS must offer a complete practice path rather than block learning when deployment is inappropriate.

sources.subject: investment-readiness
sources.title: An essential guide to building an emergency fund
sources.teaches: Emergency savings as a cash reserve for unplanned expenses, why financial shocks can create lasting debt, and how an appropriate reserve target depends on the person's situation.
sources.limitation: The source deliberately gives no universal reserve amount. OPS must not invent a mandatory number or use it as a scored investing-eligibility threshold.

sources.subject: allocation-method
sources.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Office of Investor Education and Advocacy
sources.title: Gauge Your Risk Tolerance
sources.teaches: Connects investment risk to goal, time horizon, loss of principal, and the investor's ability to tolerate volatility.
sources.limitation: It does not supply a mechanical stock-allocation formula. OPS must keep ability to bear loss separate from willingness and must not turn a questionnaire result into a recommendation.

sources.subject: allocation-method
sources.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Office of Investor Education and Advocacy
sources.title: Beginners' Guide to Asset Allocation, Diversification, and Rebalancing
sources.teaches: Time horizon, risk tolerance, strategic asset allocation, diversification, and three ways to restore target weights: trade, add to underweights, or redirect contributions.
sources.limitation: Examples explain mechanisms, not a universal allocation or drift threshold. OPS policies must expose their assumptions and costs.

sources.subject: ips-benchmark
sources.title: Elements of an Investment Policy Statement for Individual Investors
sources.teaches: The canonical section-by-section structure of an individual IPS. Sections verified present in the extracted text: Scope and Purpose, Governance, Investment/Return/Risk Objectives, Risk Management, Rebalancing, Benchmark. This is the target shape of the final dossier.

sources.subject: allocation-inputs
sources.title: Equity Risk Premiums: Determinants, Estimation and Implications
sources.teaches: Implied versus historical equity risk premium, and why the choice changes every expected return downstream. Same author as the core course, which keeps required-return work continuous with session 3.

sources.subject: allocation-inputs
sources.title: Country Default Spreads and Risk Premiums
sources.teaches: Country risk premiums for allocating outside the home market. HTML, so the figures are extractable as text rather than trapped in a spreadsheet.

sources.subject: allocation-inputs
sources.title: Historical Returns on Stocks, Bonds and Bills (US)
sources.teaches: Long-run asset-class return and risk inputs for the allocation.
sources.limitation: Legacy .xls. The source pipeline downloads and hashes it but does not extract spreadsheet cells. It was inspected during the 2026-08-12 practical-tools research with a temporary spreadsheet reader; any learner-facing use still needs a canonical cell-level extraction/provenance method or an equivalent official HTML source.

sources.subject: active-passive-base-rates
sources.title: US Active/Passive Barometer: June 2026
sources.teaches: Current category-specific, net-of-fees active-fund success rates against investable passive peers, with survivorship and fee-quintile evidence for Mission 10's evidence hurdle.
sources.limitation: Semiannual empirical scorecard. Re-fetch on each release, date every figure, preserve category and horizon, and do not turn an aggregate base rate into a claim that every active strategy fails.

sources.subject: risk-adjusted-evidence
sources.title: The Sharpe Ratio
sources.urlNote: Official author-hosted HTML reprint from The Journal of Portfolio Management, Fall 1994.
sources.teaches: The original author's definitions of ex ante and ex post Sharpe ratios, benchmark-relative differential return, time-period dependence, and the correlation limits of a one-number risk-adjusted comparison.
sources.limitation: Foundational methodology, not current evidence of manager persistence. Use it to define and qualify a risk-adjusted evidence test, not as a contemporary scorecard.

sources.subject: fund-etf-diligence
sources.title: Mutual Funds and Exchange-Traded Funds (investor.gov)
sources.teaches: The regulator's own framing of fund structures, fees and risks — the vocabulary a prospectus assumes.

sources.subject: order-rehearsal
sources.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Office of Investor Education and Advocacy
sources.title: Investor Bulletin: Understanding Order Types
sources.teaches: Market, limit, and stop-order mechanics and the trade-offs between execution certainty and price control.
sources.limitation: OPS uses this for an order rehearsal only. It must never transmit an order or imply that one order type is universally best.

sources.subject: order-rehearsal
sources.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Office of Investor Education and Advocacy
sources.title: Investor Bulletin: How to Open a Brokerage Account
sources.teaches: Cash-versus-margin account differences, account-opening information, objectives, risk tolerance, fees, and confirmation responsibilities.
sources.limitation: The course must default its rehearsal to cash and treat margin as a warning, not a beginner feature. Account eligibility and authority can vary with the learner.

sources.subject: tax-accounts
sources.title: Publication 550: Investment Income and Expenses
sources.teaches: Dividends, interest, capital gain and loss treatment, holding periods, wash sales. The tax half of the friction budget.

sources.subject: tax-accounts
sources.title: Publication 590-A: Contributions to Individual Retirement Arrangements
sources.teaches: Account types and contribution rules — the container decision that precedes asset location.

sources.subject: tax-accounts
sources.title: Publication 590-B: Distributions from Individual Retirement Arrangements
sources.teaches: Withdrawal rules and timing, which constrain the horizon and liquidity claims made in mission 1.

endpoints.subject: fund-etf-diligence
endpoints.title: EDGAR company submissions API
endpoints.urlNote: Liveness probe against Vanguard Index Funds (CIK 36405). The bare cgi-bin path returns 403 without query parameters; verified working endpoints are data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK{10-digit}.json, cgi-bin/browse-edgar with action+CIK+type, and efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index.
endpoints.requiredHeader: SEC policy requires a User-Agent identifying the requester with contact details. Requests without one are refused.
endpoints.teaches: Real prospectuses (485BPOS), portfolio holdings (N-PORT) and annual reports (N-CEN). The primary artifact for fund diligence, and it reuses OPS's existing filing-reader pattern.

designBoundaries.subject: personal-position-sizing
designBoundaries.status: No universal SEC or FINRA personal position-size cap exists. Investment-company and RIC diversification tests govern fund classification or tax status and must not be presented as personal suitability rules.
designBoundaries.method: Use FINRA's concentration-risk categories for look-through, then derive a candidate ceiling transparently from position weight × assumed position loss = contribution to portfolio loss. Label every numerical threshold as an OPS/learner policy and validate it through the Mission 5 stress test.
